A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DCoLT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison, including matching renamed models and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original DCoLT experiments on Sudoku, mathematical reasoning and code generation, together with ablations and generation-process analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds difficulty-specific MATH results, a matched LoRA comparison, Dream-7B training results and a training-reward curve.

M1.justification: The DCoLT action definitions, reinforcement-learning objective, Algorithm 1 and UPM architecture remain unchanged. LLaDOU names the existing DCoLT-trained LLaDA with UPM; the additional LoRA and Dream experiments do not introduce new DCoLT algorithm steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use Sudoku 4×4, GSM8K-Aug, GSM8K, MATH, KodCode, MBPP and HumanEval. The new experiments reuse existing tasks and data; MATH difficulty breakdowns and different model configurations do not introduce new task or population coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing comparisons retain their comparator membership. V3's additional matched comparison uses LLaDA, diffu-GRPO and d1-LLaDA, already compared in v1; Dream-7B also already appears in Table 2. The additions change experimental configurations rather than comparator methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2.3 adds a GSM8K-only comparison using LoRA rank 128 and scaling factor 64, with generation length 256, 128 diffusion steps and block length 32. Appendix C.2.4 adds a Dream-7B experiment with 64 steps and length 256. Table 3 adds difficulty-stratified evaluation, including length 128. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: V3 Table 3 extends the existing generation-length analysis by separating MATH difficulty levels, and Figure 12 adds a training-dynamics diagnostic. The UPM, adaptive-layer-normalization and block-length ablations, along with the existing reasoning case studies, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark results. V3's raw and moving-average reward curves describe training trends, not uncertainty across independent runs.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. V3 adds MATH difficulty-by-length results, GSM8K LoRA accuracies of 84.7% for LLaDOU versus 79.8% for diffu-GRPO and 81.1% for d1-LLaDA, and Dream-7B results increasing from 50.11% to 80.53% within the new experiment. These are additional settings, not revisions to Table 2 scores. Figure 12 also adds reward-trajectory results.

T1.justification: The diffusion-process definitions, transition-probability derivations, Plackett–Luce unmasking policy and combined action probabilities in Equations 1–9 are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: reinforcing intermediate diffusion actions, using an unmasking policy for LLaDA, and improving mathematical reasoning and code generation. The headline performance claims are unchanged; the added experiments provide supporting evidence.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new MATH breakdown as showing saturation around length 256 for easy problems while harder problems benefit from longer responses. Appendix C.2.4 interprets the Dream results as evidence of applicability across different diffusion architectures. Existing resource and verifiable-reward limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly describes Sudoku reward checks and boxed-answer extraction with symbolic-equivalence checking for GSM8K/MATH. It documents LoRA and Dream training settings and adds a repository link. These reward details do not establish changes to the earlier implementation; Appendix F still promises a future release, so actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds Shi et al., Simplified and generalized masked diffusion for discrete data, to the introduction and related-work discussion. The positioning against CoT, DoT and earlier diffusion-model reinforcement learning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 standardizes the LLaDOU name, corrects wording and SEDD spelling, expands affiliations, adds acknowledgements and conference information, and inserts Appendix C.2.3–C.2.4. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the difficulty-by-length table, the matched LoRA comparison table and the reward-curve figure. Existing displays are retained with caption edits, relocation and renumbering; notably, v1 Figure 12 becomes v3 Figure 13. The original appendix raster images are identical.

improvement.justification: The matched LoRA/GSM8K comparison addresses a comparability weakness in v1, while the Dream experiment, difficulty breakdown and explicit reward-checking details improve empirical support and reproducibility. These are limited gains to an otherwise stable paper. A new reporting problem tempers the improvement: Figure 12 shows negative raw rewards without reconciling them with the stated 0/1 reward scheme.
